model.entity: A continuously tracked object (e.g. GPT-6, Claude Code, ZCode, CVE-2026-94127)
model.event: A specific change that happened to an entity (e.g. release, pricing change, version update, CISA KEV addition)
model.observation: A discovery or report of an Event by a Radar/Source
rules: Multiple observations may map to one event
Multiple events may belong to one entity
Different canonicalEventType for same entity = different event (no cross-type UPDATE)
lowercase
deterministic
no random UUID
human debuggable
machine comparable
canonicalEventType is part of identity — different types never share eventKey

eventTypeRegistry.model-release: AI model publication or weight release
eventTypeRegistry.research-release: Research paper, study, or project published
eventTypeRegistry.version-update: Version bump of an existing tool or library
eventTypeRegistry.pricing-change: Pricing, availability, or licensing terms change
eventTypeRegistry.capability-change: New feature or capability added to existing product
eventTypeRegistry.security-advisory: Non-CVE security advisory or vulnerability disclosure

removedTypes.tool-discovery: Removed — discovery is observation metadata, not an event type. Merged into release.

order: version-update: version string extractable AND entity already tracked
release: everything else (including first discovery of new tools)
rules: Precedence is determined by entity type and available version info, not title wording
First discovery of a new tool = release (not a discovery event type)
Claude Code 2.1.281 = version-update (version string present, entity tracked)
New model first published = model-release
New skill first published = skill-release

eventIdentifierPrecedence.description: CVE ID extracted from title (e.g. CVE-2026-94493)

canonicalization.entity: Normalize to lowercase kebab-case slug. Common variants of same entity must map to same slug.
canonicalization.version: Extract numeric version string (major.minor.patch) from title. Ignore 'v' prefix.
canonicalization.url: Normalize: strip trailing slash, strip query params (except canonical article IDs).

examples.entity: ZCode / ZCode - Z.ai / Z.ai ZCode -> zcode

NEW.definition: eventKey has never been seen in the registry

DUPLICATE.definition: eventKey exists AND no material change detected

UPDATE.definition: eventKey exists AND material change detected within same canonicalEventType
UPDATE.boundaryRule: If canonicalEventType changed, it is a NEW event, not UPDATE. Cross-type progression (e.g. security-cve -> security-cisa-kev) = two separate events.

minimalMaterialChange.scope: Phase 5A minimal. Full Material Change Engine is Phase 5B.
isUpdate: new version (version string differs from registry, within version-update)
exploitation status changed (activeExploitation false -> true or vice versa)
major capability change (new model size, new platform)
isNotUpdate: media coverage increased or additional source reporting same event
same claim from another source (accumulate into sources[])
minimalMaterialChange.crossTypeRule: canonicalEventType change = NEW event, never UPDATE

fingerprint.strategy: SHA256 over event facts only. User-relative intelligence metadata excluded.

excludedFields.securityGate: User-relative assessment of relevance, not an event fact
excludedFields.title: Text content, not structural

fingerprint.hashInput: JSON stringification of sorted field names with non-null values
rules: Null or absent fields are excluded
Fingerprint comparison is exact match only
Fingerprint change implies potential material change
Text fields are NEVER in fingerprint
User-relative assessment fields are NEVER in fingerprint

observationModel.definition: An Observation is a discovery or report of an Event by a Radar/Source

schema.eventKey: string (the event this observation maps to)

rules: One Event may have multiple Observations
Multiple Observations of same Event = sources[] accumulation, not new events
Observation metadata (title, description) does not affect Event identity

sourceDedup.principle: Multiple sources reporting same eventKey = one event with multiple sources[]
rules: First source sets firstSeen
Subsequent sources append to sources[]
Duplicate source URL = ignored

registry.separationRule: Event Facts and Intelligence Metadata are stored separately. Intelligence metadata changes do NOT create Event UPDATE.

radarBoundary.phase5a: Event Identity, Same-event Dedup, Minimal UPDATE boundary
radarBoundary.phase5b: Full Material Change Engine, semantic diff, importance delta, event lifecycle
radarBoundary.phase5c: Primary Radar Ownership, Cross-Radar Collision Resolution, relatedRadars

overMergeGuard.rule: Same entity does NOT imply same event. Different canonicalEventType = different event.
examples: GPT-6 model-release and GPT-6 pricing-change = two events
Claude Code version-update and Claude Code incident = two events
F5 BIG-IP security-cve and F5 BIG-IP security-cisa-kev = two events (resolved)
Atuin release on day 1 and Atuin release re-reported on day 2 = one event (DUPLICATE)

ambiguousFallback.principle: Prefer false split over false merge. Two events temporarily separate is lower risk than swallowing a real new event.
ambiguousFallback.behavior: When identity is ambiguous, default to treating as DUPLICATE only if eventKey matches exactly. If there is any doubt about entity or identifier mapping, treat as NEW.

loggedCases.phase5bNeeded: Full pricing terms comparison to determine if material change
